# Loom Agent V0.3 — Full Agent Context

> Use this file to orient a coding agent before modifying Loom. It consolidates the current architecture, commands, contracts, invariants, and limitations. Source code and tests remain authoritative.

## Project purpose

Loom is a CLI-first durable harness for one developer agent. V0.3 focuses on completing measurable work through a persisted task graph and reviewer-gated verification. Do not add multi-agent orchestration, swarm behavior, web/desktop UI, a scheduler, daemon, distributed state, vector memory, or embeddings in this milestone.

## Runtime requirements

- Node.js 22+ for the built-in SQLite runtime.
- Bun 1.x for workspace installation and development commands.
- Git for repository inspection and diff checks.

Primary commands:

```bash
bun install
npm run build
bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts
npm run eval
npm run loom -- run "fix all failing tests"
```

## Repository packages

- `@loom/core`: shared data and interface contracts.
- `@loom/state`: SQLite runtime, migrations, and durable queries.
- `@loom/planner`: plan templates, dependency scheduling, execute/verify phases, retry and recovery.
- `@loom/tools`: normalized tools, permission/approval middleware, idempotency ledger, native tools.
- `@loom/providers`: deterministic mock and OpenAI-compatible adapters.
- `@loom/mcp`: basic line-delimited stdio MCP adapter.
- `@loom/context`: priority-based character-budget compiler used by the compatibility runtime.
- `@loom/skills`: `.loom/skills/*/SKILL.md` discovery and parsing.
- `@loom/runtime`: V0.2-compatible `AgentLoop`.
- `@loom/evals`: stable deterministic orchestration scenarios.
- `@loom/cli`: configuration, dependency wiring, commands, and output.

Dependency direction should flow from CLI to concrete packages, planner to state/core, and state to core. Keep CLI code out of reusable packages.

## V0.3 execution model

`loom run <goal>` creates an agent and calls `PlanEngine.create`. Coding goals matching `fix|test|bug|code|parser` receive:

```text
Inspect repository
-> Run tests
-> Diagnose failures
-> Fix implementation
-> Run targeted tests
-> Run full suite
-> Review diff
```

Other goals receive `Inspect goal -> Execute goal -> Verify result`.

`TaskGraphRuntime.runnable` makes a pending task ready only when all dependencies completed. Failed or blocked dependencies block downstream tasks. `VerifiedExecutionRuntime` executes ready tasks and uses a separate `Reviewer` for verification tasks.

Reviewer rejection reopens the direct dependency while retry budget remains, puts verification back to pending, creates a checkpoint, and traces `verification.rejected`. The plan becomes completed only when every task is completed.

## Lifecycle types

Agent statuses:

```text
created running waiting paused recovering completed failed stopped
```

Task statuses:

```text
pending ready running waiting blocked completed failed needs_approval
```

Phases:

```text
plan execute verify
```

Failure policies:

```text
retryable non_retryable blocked needs_approval needs_human
```

`retryable` returns a task to ready within its budget. `needs_approval` moves task to `needs_approval` and agent/plan to waiting. `deny` fails without replay. `needs_human` blocks automated progress.

## Persistence

Default database: `.loom/loom.db`. Override with `LOOM_DB`.

Migrations:

1. `agents`, `traces`, `checkpoints`
2. `working_memory`, `tool_execution_ledger`
3. `plans`, `plan_tasks`, `approval_requests`, `artifacts`
4. `task_checkpoints`

Task checkpoints have `cp_...` ids and store agent, plan, task, phase, step, JSON snapshot, and timestamp. Artifacts link to agent, task, and checkpoint. Existing databases are upgraded with append-only migration records.

Never rewrite an applied migration. Add a new numbered migration and regression coverage.

## Recovery and idempotency

`loom resume <agent-id>` reloads the newest plan. Completed tasks are not rerun. Approved tasks return to ready. Denied tasks fail without execution.

Tool calls with ids are recorded before execution. A succeeded result is reused. An `executing` or `unknown` state is not replayed automatically because side effects may already have happened.

`--max-tasks <n>` is a deterministic pause mechanism for testing recovery; it is not an operating-system crash injector.

## Tools and approvals

Native tools are `read_file`, `write_file`, and `shell`. All normalized provider and MCP calls go through `ToolExecutor`.

Permission values:

- `allow`: execute.
- `deny`: fail non-retryably.
- `ask`: create a durable request and throw `ApprovalRequiredError`.

Approval commands:

```bash
loom approvals [agent-id]
loom approve <request-id>
loom deny <request-id>
loom resume <agent-id>
```

Native paths are resolved against the workspace and checked after real-path resolution for reads and parent resolution for writes. Shell uses an explicit working directory, timeout, capture limit, and reports exit/duration. It still runs through an OS shell and is not sandboxed.

## Providers

The default `MockProvider` is deterministic and does not repair real code. Set `LOOM_PROVIDER=openai` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the real adapter. `LOOM_MODEL` overrides the config model. `OPENAI_BASE_URL` selects another compatible endpoint.

The OpenAI-compatible adapter uses Chat Completions, is non-streaming, and normalizes output/tool calls/usage/finish reason/request id/model. V0.3 supports one tool round followed by one final provider call.

Normal tests must not require credentials or network access.

## Configuration

Project config is `.loom/config.json`; start with `.loom/config.example.json`. Environment overrides project config for provider/model. There are no `--provider` or `--model` flags.

Supported fields:

```json
{
  "provider": "mock",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "context": {"maxChars": 50000},
  "permissions": {"read_file": "allow", "write_file": "ask", "shell": "ask"},
  "mcpServers": {}
}
```

`context.maxChars` applies to the compatibility `AgentLoop`, not V0.3 graph task prompts.

## CLI

Commands: `run`, `ps`, `inspect`, `resume`, `trace`, `approvals`, `approve`, `deny`, `skills`, `skills show`, `tools`, `memory`, `memory set`, `memory delete`, and `config`.

Global parsed options: `--json`, `--max-tasks`, and `--skill`. V0.3 parses `--skill` but does not yet inject it into graph execution.

Inspect must expose goal/status/phase, ordered tasks, current task, latest checkpoint, and artifacts. JSON output also includes approvals and durable records.

## Skills and context

Skills live in `.loom/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with simple frontmatter: `name`, `description`, and inline comma-separated `tools`. V0.3 graph execution discovers skills but does not enforce selected skill instructions/tool lists. Do not claim otherwise.

The `ContextCompiler` priority order is system, goal, runtime, skills, memory, tools, recovery, messages, and files. It truncates lower-priority content under a character budget and preserves required goal/tool sources where possible. This path belongs to the V0.2-compatible runtime.

## MCP

MCP config defines command, args, and env. Loom spawns stdio servers, initializes, lists tools, and adapts `tools/call` results. Failures do not remove native tools.

V0.3 lacks HTTP/SSE transports, request timeout, reconnection, cancellation, and a full lifecycle manager. MCP processes inherit Loom environment and are not sandboxed.

## Tracing

Key graph events: `agent.created`, `plan.created`, `task.started`, `task.completed`, `task.retrying`, `verification.passed`, `verification.rejected`, `checkpoint.created`, `agent.paused`, `agent.recovering`, `plan.completed`, `approval.approved`, `approval.denied`.

Trace payloads are not automatically secret-redacted.

## Evaluation

`npm run eval` runs six stable scenarios: failing-test repair, file creation, multi-file modification, crash/resume, failed verification, and denied tool call. They use in-memory SQLite and deterministic test doubles. They test orchestration invariants, not model quality or genuine repository repair.

## Required checks

Before review:

```bash
npm run build
bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts
npm run eval
git diff --check
```

Also manually verify `run --max-tasks`, `inspect`, `resume`, and an `ask -> approve/deny -> resume` flow when those areas change.

## Known limitations

- Rule-based plan templates.
- Targeted verification currently runs the full Vitest suite.
- Diff review is `git diff --check` plus `git diff --stat`, not semantic review.
- One provider tool round, no streaming.
- Skills not injected/enforced in graph execution.
- Basic stdio-only MCP.
- Local unsigned approvals.
- Synchronous, single-process SQLite.
- Partial artifact discovery rather than complete filesystem-diff derivation.
- Deterministic evals are not intelligence benchmarks.
- No sandbox or general secret redaction.

Do not begin multi-agent work until planning, recovery, verification, approvals, and real-world eval coverage are stronger.
